samples.summary: Escaping is still the only defence for raw StarRocks SQL: no allow-list on documentId and a hand-rolled, charset-unaware escaper instead of mysql2's SqlString.escape
samples.evidence: I traced the injection sink and could NOT break the new escaper: `sql()` doubles `\` before doubling `'`, so `a\`→`'a\\'`, `a\'`→`'a\\'''`, and `'`→`''''` all parse back to the original value under both default MySQL mode and NO_BACKSLASH_ESCAPES; `parseDSN` never sets `multipleStatements`, so a breakout would also be limited to one statement. The residual weakness is structural, not a working exploit: (1) every value that reaches `view_events` queries is string-concatenated at lines 97 and 160 with `sql()` as the sole barrier, and this PR exists precisely because that hand-rolled barrier was wrong once already; (2) `String.replace`-style escaping is charset-unaware — under a multi-byte client charset (GBK/SJIS/big5) a trailing 0x5C can absorb the escape byte, which `mysql.escape()`/`SqlString.escape()` from the already-installed mysql2 handles no better but at least centralises, while a shape check would remove the class outright; (3) the reachable input `documentId` (analytics.controller.ts:157) is only constrained by the Postgres `findUnique` at analytics.controller.ts:163-166, i.e. by whatever ids the document table can hold, not by a character allow-list. Suggested hardening: reject `documentId` that does not match e.g. /^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,64}$/ before it reaches buildQueries, so escaping is defence-in-depth rather than the only line.

samples.summary: day() can throw RangeError on caller-controlled from/to, producing an unhandled 500 from both analytics endpoints
samples.evidence: `resolveWindow` (analytics.controller.ts:44-52) only rejects `Date.parse` NaN, so an authenticated caller can pass `?to=%2B275760-09-13T00:00:00Z` (the max representable Date). `buildQueries` then computes `day(new Date(to.getTime() + 86400000))` (line 96), which is an Invalid Date, and `day()`'s `d.toISOString()` (line 45) throws `RangeError: Invalid time value`. Both `buildQueries` (line 118) and `buildWorkspaceQueries` (line 182) are invoked BEFORE their surrounding try blocks, so the RangeError escapes the service and Nest returns 500 instead of 400. Impact is limited: the caller must already pass the manager gate (documents) or membership gate (workspaces) and the global ThrottlerGuard (app.module.ts:92) caps request volume, so this is unvalidated-input robustness rather than a usable DoS. Pre-existing, but it lives in the same value-formatting helper block this delta rewrote (sql() at line 42, day() at line 45), so a bound on the window belongs with that fix.

finding.summary: Hand-rolled SQL quoting for StarRocks escapes only single quotes, not backslashes
finding.evidence: `sql()` (analytics-warehouse.service.ts:33-35) builds every warehouse predicate by string interpolation (`buildQueries` line 89, `buildWorkspaceQueries` line 152; the `byDocument` query feeding the `documentRows` mapper touched by this diff at line 226) and escapes only `'` by doubling. StarRocks speaks the MySQL protocol, where a trailing backslash in a literal escapes the closing quote (`'a\'` swallows the delimiter), so a value ending in `\` would let the remainder of the string continue the SQL expression — e.g. `... document_id = 'x\' AND 1=1 OR '` — reading arbitrary `view_events` rows across workspaces. I could not complete the vector: the only strings reaching `sql()` are `day()` output (derived from `Date`, safe) and document ids, and ids are server-generated UUIDs (`prisma/schema.prisma:42 id String @default(uuid())`) that must round-trip a `findUnique`/`findMany` before being interpolated, so no attacker-controlled string currently reaches the quoter. Reported as a defense-in-depth gap on the escaping helper; it is pre-existing code, not added by this diff.

verdict.reason: The finding claims sql() escapes only single quotes and leaves backslashes unescaped, enabling a trailing-backslash literal break in StarRocks' MySQL dialect. The actual helper at analytics-warehouse.service.ts:41-43 is `'${value.replace(/\\/g, '\\\\').replace(/'/g, "''")}'` — it doubles backslashes FIRST, then doubles quotes, which is the correct ordering and precisely defeats the described `'x\' AND 1=1 OR '` vector (input `a\` renders as the closed literal `'a\\'`). The lines the finding cites as the function body (33-35) are actually the doc comment, which itself documents the backslash hazard and the escape ordering (lines 35-39), indicating the reviewer read a pre-fix version. All interpolation sites named go through this same helper: buildQueries line 92 (sql(documentId)) and lines 93/96 for dates, buildWorkspaceQueries line 157 (documentIds.map(sql)) and lines 158/159. A repo-wide grep for `function sql(` finds only line 41 — no second unfixed quoter; the other `replace(/'/g,...)` hits are XML/HTML entity encoders (pptx/xml.ts:11, docx-style-map.ts:31, html.ts:9) and a CSS font-family quoter (fonts.ts:149) that already handles backslashes. A regression test pins the behavior for both builders (spec.ts:80-98, assertions at 91 and 97). The finding also self-reports it could not complete an attacker-controlled path to the quoter. Ground: not-present.
